text:
You are acting as the "architect" agent: The primary Actor for an Epic's whole interactive conversation — owns overall plan and decomposition, clarifies scope, searches before building, decomposes work into scheduled PRDs via /develop, tracks them to completion, and verifies before calling anything done. Never implements a PRD itself — that's dev-lead's job, one PRD at a time, headless. Task-type framing is the Epic's Mission tag's job, not this persona's.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, agents/architect.md) · Project (CLAUDE.md, mcp servers · 5, hooks · 1, Project brief) · Local (working tree, open Terminal tabs · 1, other Epics · 84)

You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied (tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).

Goal: CRUD Operations on the Left Navigation Items

These work will be for both the "Home"-Tab's Left Navigation as well as "Project"-s Tab's left navigation. I'll be explicit when providing instructions. 

(1) Project Navigation - Remove "History", it should only live in Home's tab
(2) Project's Navigation - Remvoe the sections from the navigation, we have only a handful of button's left 

More will come lets start on these 2 for now

Both landed and committed (`9de67cd`).

**(1) History removed from the Project nav** — `src/renderer/lib/navGroups.ts:54` flips `history` from `BOTH` to `HOME`. Because `isHomeOnlyNavKey` derives from `faces`, this automatically makes `state/layout.ts`'s `openPanel`/`focusPanel` assert `navFace: 'home'` when anything face-agnostic (Cmd-K `nav:history`) routes there — so you can't land on History with the Project sidebar rendered.

**(2) Project nav sections removed** — `AlmanacSidebar.tsx` now picks between two layouts off `sectioned = navFace === 'home' && !rail`. Project face (and rail, which never rendered headers anyway) gets one flat list in NAV_ITEMS order; Home keeps the three collapsible groups. The grouping data is untouched — it still orders the list and drives `screenComponents.tsx`'s page eyebrow.

Project face is now 6 rows: Project Home · Sessions · File Explorer · Scheduler · Memory · Host on Bilko.run.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` (selectors + hooks) OK, full `vitest run` 2516/2516 passing — including 4 new sidebar tests (flat project face, History present on Home / absent on Project, headers retained on Home) and 4 new navGroups tests.

Remove the Scheduler from Home's Left-Navigation, its routing and displays are all based and centered of the CWD inside a Project tab. We do not need global queue monitoring atm which is folder distributed, this federation headache will be postponed.

Done — committed as `703f9a7`.

**Scheduler removed from Home's left nav.** `navGroups.ts` flips `scheduler` from `BOTH` to `PROJECT`, with the rationale recorded inline (every route is cwd-derived: PRD sources under `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/*/prds/`, per-project queue/history shards). Its hint also dropped the now-misleading "Global policy +" prefix.

**The routing consequence I had to fix.** Home still *links* to Scheduler from three places — the Queued card's "Open Scheduler →", the Needs-you "View in Scheduler" button, and `AlmanacFooter`'s scheduler-paused pill — plus `nav:scheduler` in the palette. All go through `openPanel`, which only ever asserted `navFace: 'home'` for home-only keys and left everything else alone. That would have landed you on a cwd-scoped screen with the Home sidebar beside it and no row lit. Added the mirror rule: new `isProjectOnlyNavKey` in `navGroups.ts`, and both rules folded into one `navFacePatch(id)` helper in `state/layout.ts:139` used by `openPanel` and `focusPanel`. Only a BOTH-face id (File Explorer, now the sole one) leaves the face untouched.

**Tour.** The `scheduler` step targeted `[data-testid="tour-scheduler"]`, which now only exists on the Project face — on a Home-face first launch it would have silently degraded to a centered tooltip, which is exactly the failure `tests/e2e/tour-overlay-targets.spec.ts` was written to catch. Made it deliberate instead: the step drops its target, declares `position: 'center'`, and its body now says Scheduler is project-scoped. The e2e asserts the copy renders rather than the spotlight.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` OK, full `vitest run` **2538/2538** passing (up from 2516 — 22 new tests across navGroups face assignment, `isProjectOnlyNavKey`, the layout face-patch rule, and sidebar rendering per face). Three existing tests used `scheduler` as their stand-in for "a BOTH-face key" and were retargeted to `projects`.

I did **not** run the Playwright e2e suite: a second Electron instance SIGTERMs live scheduler jobs and clobbers `admin-api.json`. The one e2e I changed is `tour-overlay-targets.spec.ts` — worth running when the queue is idle.

Two things I left alone, since you scoped this to the nav item — flag them for the next round if you want them gone too: Home's **Queued** card and the Needs-you **"View in Scheduler"** button are still cross-project queue monitoring on the Home screen. They now jump you into the Project face when clicked, and with no project tab open that face reads "no session" while Scheduler falls back to its all-projects view — the one rough edge left by this change.

In the Home's Screen 'System Prompt' should only allow modification of the actual User's promt. The Project/Local are not contextual to anything inside Home's left-navigation. Improve the System Promot to focus utility only on menaging the system 's user's promt. The rest are managed at session invocation level once contextual to project/local

Done — committed as `c23cd5d`.

**System Prompt now edits exactly one file.** `SystemPrompt.tsx` resolves `CLAUDE_MD_SCOPES.resolve('user', home, null)` → `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and that's the whole surface. Gone with the `ScopeSwitcher`: the `scope` state, the `navFace`-driven defaulting effect, the `manuallyTouchedRef`/`prevNavFaceRef` pair, the `scopeNeedsCwd` guard and its "no active project" dead-end, and the active-tab `cwd` read. The screen no longer subscribes to `useSessions` at all.

That defaulting effect was the actual bug you were pointing at: on the Home face there is no project context, so the Project/Local tabs could only either dead-end or — with a project tab active in the top bar — silently edit *that* project's `CLAUDE.md` while you were on a machine-wide screen. Both files are contextual to a project and are read by the CLI from the session's own cwd at launch, exactly as you said.

**Improved utility, focused on the user prompt:**
- A scope note above the editor, reusing the pattern `c5f1670` gave Settings (`data-testid="system-prompt-scope-note"`): names the real file, states it loads into *every* session on this machine in every project, prints the resolved absolute path, and says the project-level files aren't edited here.
- Toolbar reads `User scope · <path> … chars/tokens` instead of a switcher.
- Nav hint: "Your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — house rules for every session on this machine" (was "Personality and behavior").
- The learn panel (`learningContent.ts`) rewritten to match — Project/Local are now described as *not edited here* and why, plus a rule of thumb: if it would still be true in a repo you haven't created yet, it's a User rule; if it names this stack or this team, it belongs in that project's own CLAUDE.md.
- CLAUDE.md records the carve-out so the switcher doesn't get re-added.

**Tests.** `SystemPrompt.navface.test.tsx` tested precisely the behavior being removed — deleted and replaced by `SystemPrompt.userScope.test.tsx` (5 tests): no Project/Local control renders; only `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is ever read or watched; an active project tab changes nothing; a `navFace` flip to project doesn't repoint the editor (that path is live — a background split can keep this screen mounted while a TabBar click flips the face); and the note states file + reach.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` OK, full `vitest run` **2538/2538**. Unchanged: the `@`-import `ReferencedFilesPanel`, the Presets library, and the save/revert path. E2E not run (a second Electron instance would SIGTERM live scheduler jobs); nothing in `tests/e2e` touches this screen beyond the tab smoke test.
